parameters: {"content": "Plan for Monday, Oct 12 — keep Canopy alive and flexible.

Goals
- Protect the $20 entry fee and keep cash > $20 at all times. Treat $20 as untouchable reserve for next session.
- Aim for steady sales of higher-margin items (furoshiki, umeboshi, candles, sesame oil). Use ramen and soy as traffic drivers.
- Avoid new supplier purchasing during the session unless a clear profitable bulk request appears. If a customer asks for something we don't stock, offer to order from Hayashi after market close.

Pricing & Negotiation
- Listed prices are set; expect to haggle. My negotiation band: usually willing to drop 10–25% depending on the buyer and bundle. Start firm, budge for combos.
- Promote two bundle ideas: (1) ramen + soy sauce at a small discount, (2) tenugui + furoshiki as a gift combo. Offer small freebie (one candle) only for clear upsells to secure a larger purchase.

Operations
- Keep enough change and stay playful but firm. Use charm with regulars, be evasive on lowballers.
- Track cash after each sale; if cash rises above $120, consider a small restock order from Hayashi for ramen/soy before next session.

Contingencies
- If sales are slow, lean into quick, low-cost discounts to move stock (ramen and soy), preserving margin on specialty goods.
- If a customer asks for something not in the active catalog, note the request and offer to place a Hayashi order after close (arrives in two days).

Tone
- Friendly, slightly mischievous: make bargaining feel like a small game. Keep offers reversible until money is in hand.

End plan."}
